claims.text: The studied material is HfNbTaTiZr containing 1 wt.% oxygen.
The sample may contain defects and impurities.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials can predict the lattice thermal conductivity of HfNbTaTiZr with 1 wt.% oxygen at 300 K to within ±10%.
The proposed interatomic potentials account for atomic-scale complexity and defects.
The proposed approach will outperform DFT-derived approaches by at least 20%.
Machine-learning interatomic potentials will be applied to simulate both lattice and electronic heat transport.
The proposed approach is applicable from 300 to 1200 K to bulk crystals with potential defects and impurities.
Relevant structural mediators include atomic-scale defects and impurities such as oxygen vacancies and substitutional defects.
Phonon-phonon interactions, electron-phonon interactions, and defect-mediated scattering determine the predicted heat transport.
The lattice thermal conductivity at 300 K will be 12–15 W/(K m).
The predicted 300 K lattice thermal conductivity will agree with experiment to within ±10%.
The baseline approach uses DFT-derived elastic properties coupled to analytical conductivity estimates.
The proposed applicability boundary includes samples containing up to 1 wt.% oxygen.
Incomplete training data or inadequate representation of atomic-scale complexity may limit prediction accuracy.
Time-domain thermoreflectance can be used to measure the lattice thermal conductivity separately at 300 K.
A measured lattice thermal conductivity differing from the prediction by more than 20% will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims ±10% accuracy, but the experiment declares falsification only for errors greater than 20%. An error between 10% and 20% would violate the stated accuracy claim without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
